title: 5.2L 32V Ti-VCT Intake Air Distribution and Filtering: Overview
introduction: The intake has separate cleaning and measuring jobs. I keep those roles straight: the filter handles the housekeeping, while the airflow sensor keeps the tally. This overview applies to the engine identified above and explains why scheduled filter replacement matters. Replacement access, the service interval and restriction measurements require separate service information.

edits.text: The intake system cleans incoming air with a replaceable, dry-type engine air cleaner element made from treated, pleated paper. Install a new element at the scheduled service intervals. When the element reaches its maximum restriction, engine performance and fuel economy suffer.
edits.why: The element's ability to pass air matters as well as its cleaning role. Scheduled replacement addresses this service item; the stated restriction consequence explains why leaving it indefinitely can cost both performance and economy.

edits.text: The MAF (mass air flow) sensor measures the airflow entering the engine.
edits.why: I distinguish the sensor's measuring role from the air cleaner element's filtering role. Understanding those separate jobs helps make sense of the intake system without assuming that either component has failed.
